findings.body: The toolbar check runs during the Vite build: Vite statically replaces `import.meta.env` values ([Vite documentation](https://vite.dev/guide/env-and-mode)). The scaffold Dockerfile builds the frontend at `src/forge/templates/skeleton/Dockerfile:6` without passing `APP_ENV` into that build. Setting `APP_ENV=demo` when the demo container starts cannot restore the omitted toolbar. The convention needs an explicit demo build that supplies the value at build time, alongside a production build that excludes it.
findings.title: Not done: Anyone can point at the screen

findings.body: The stack convention tells a builder to add the loader, but the unchanged Forge skill at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:103-111` does not tell the agent to build it in the prototype's first version or use `Words they use` for screen labels. This part's scope excludes the skill; SPEC is the next task that edits it.
findings.title: Later: SPEC must put first-version demo data and customer labels in the skill

findings.body: The frontend convention describes clicking an element and pasting feedback, but the unchanged Forge skill at `src/forge/templates/skill.md:103-111` gives salespeople no Agentation instructions. This part cannot edit the skill under its scope; DEMO's skill update needs to carry that instruction.
findings.title: Later: DEMO must put the pointing instructions in the skill

findings.body: The example counts tables before opening the insertion transaction. During a rolling deployment, the prior instance remains available (`src/forge/templates/conventions/deploy.md:5`); if it creates the first row after these counts, the loader can insert demo rows into a database that is no longer empty. Keep the emptiness check and insertion in one database transaction with isolation that makes a concurrent first write cause refusal or retry.
findings.title: Make the empty-table check atomic with demo insertion
